framework.title: Shared Technology Services (STS) Framework
framework.intent: Explore service management as a living lifecycle: opportunity and demand enter the system, practices and governance shape the response, services are designed, built, delivered, supported, improved, and realized as value.
framework.definition: Shared Technology Services (STS) Framework is the navigation and learning frame for this explorer. The underlying reference structures remain ITIL and IT4IT reference models: Service Value System, Service Value Chain, value streams, practice groups, practices, contribution mapping, and empty dependency structure.
framework.body: Read the model as a journey first, then use the practice catalogue as the vocabulary that explains what capabilities participate in that journey.

annotations.title: Authority boundary
annotations.body: Current reference mode preserves external standards and named disciplines in their own vocabulary, structure, and recognized meaning. Local operating-model extensions are deferred and must be modeled separately from external reference truth.

annotations.title: Ordering boundary
annotations.body: Every graph node has deterministic ordering inside its scope. External reference nodes follow reference-list ordering; where the reference provides a list but not a workflow, the order must be labeled as list order. Site navigation order is only display metadata and must not be treated as industry sequence.

annotations.title: Flow and lifecycle layer
annotations.body: Practice catalogues define vocabulary. Flow models, value streams, activities, edges, and positionings explain how service-management behavior works end to end. Current flow nodes preserve external ITIL and IT4IT reference structure only.

annotations.title: Multidimensional operating model
annotations.body: The same practice can belong to multiple industry-reference dimensions: reference catalogue, lifecycle flow, contribution map, and empty dependency graph. Local rollout, maturity, assurance, and bank-specific interpretations remain out of scope until the ITIL / ITSM / IT4IT reference abstraction is stable.

ordering.notes: Site navigation root order only; not an industry workflow, dependency, or maturity order.

model_roots.title: STS Operating Model
model_roots.intent: How STS is run across the ecosystem of shared technology services.
model_roots.definition: The operating model treats each shared service as a portfolio and governance unit. It defines scope, ownership, standards, tooling, service onboarding, funding, assurance, and improvement across many services.
model_roots.body: Use this root when asking how the bank runs STS as a capability, how services enter STS, and how cross-service governance works.

ordering.notes: STS reading order: outer operating model first.

children.title: Service Portfolio And Adoption
children.intent: Which services are shared, how they enter STS, and how adoption is tracked.
children.definition: Defines service intake, onboarding, catalog inclusion, lifecycle status, adoption signal, and cross-service visibility.

ordering.notes: Operating model domain order for first orientation.

children.title: Ownership, Governance, And Standards
children.intent: Who owns decisions, standards, exceptions, and required evidence across STS.
children.definition: Defines common decision rights, service ownership expectations, standards, exception handling, assurance needs, and operating guardrails.

ordering.notes: Operating model domain order for first orientation.

children.title: Platform And Automation Enablement
children.intent: Which common tooling and automation make STS practical at scale.
children.definition: Defines catalog, templates, CI/CD, infrastructure automation, observability links, policy checks, evidence capture, and reusable standard paths.

ordering.notes: Operating model domain order for first orientation.

children.title: Operations, Reliability, And Assurance
children.intent: How shared services are supported, observed, reviewed, and kept trustworthy.
children.definition: Defines support paths, SLO expectations, incident and problem loops, continuity expectations, operational evidence, and service review cadence.

ordering.notes: Operating model domain order for first orientation.

children.title: Portfolio Economics And Improvement
children.intent: How cost, capacity, value, prioritization, and improvement are managed across services.
children.definition: Defines budget signals, cost drivers, usage, capacity, value evidence, improvement backlog, and investment prioritization across the STS portfolio.

ordering.notes: Operating model domain order for first orientation.

model_roots.title: STS Managed Service Model
model_roots.intent: How one shared service is decomposed, understood, and managed.
model_roots.definition: The managed service model decomposes one service into managed service elements, then maps operating cycles, ITIL practices, artifacts, evidence, ownership, metrics, and maturity to those elements.
model_roots.body: Use this root when asking what a service is made of, which objects are managed, and where practices act inside the service.

ordering.notes: STS reading order: inner managed service model second.

children.title: Service Definition
children.intent: What the service is, why it exists, who owns it, and what lifecycle state it has.
children.definition: Groups service identity, purpose, owner, criticality, tier, status, consumers, scope, and service expectations.

ordering.notes: Managed service model domain order for first orientation.

children.title: Consumer Interface
children.intent: What consumers can discover, request, access, subscribe to, and use.
children.definition: Groups service offerings, request types, consumers, subscriptions, provisioned instances, support entry points, and usage expectations.

ordering.notes: Managed service model domain order for first orientation.

children.title: Delivery Structure
children.intent: What is built, changed, released, deployed, rolled back, and versioned.
children.definition: Groups components, repositories, deployment units, releases, versions, configurations, templates, pipelines, and deployment evidence.

ordering.notes: Managed service model domain order for first orientation.

children.title: Runtime Structure
children.intent: What is running, where it runs, what it depends on, and how health is known.
children.definition: Groups runtime instances, environments, dependencies, health signals, capacity signals, alerts, incidents, problems, and recovery context.

ordering.notes: Managed service model domain order for first orientation.

children.title: Control And Learning
children.intent: How the service stays controlled, evidenced, improved, and eventually retired.
children.definition: Groups controls, risks, exceptions, evidence, knowledge items, cost signals, improvement items, deprecation, migration, and retirement targets.

ordering.notes: Managed service model domain order for first orientation.

ordering.notes: ITIL management-practice group list order for reference navigation; not a workflow, dependency, or maturity sequence.

children.title: Guiding Principles

ordering.notes: Reference system component order. This is not a workflow sequence.

children.title: Governance

ordering.notes: Reference system component order. This is not a workflow sequence.

children.title: Service Value Chain

ordering.notes: Reference system component order. This is not a workflow sequence.

children.title: Practices

ordering.notes: Reference system component order. This is not a workflow sequence.

children.title: Continual Improvement

ordering.notes: Reference system component order. This is not a workflow sequence.

children.title: Value

model_dimensions.title: Reference Catalogue
model_dimensions.intent: Shows what practices exist and how the reference catalogue is listed.
model_dimensions.notes: This dimension is not a workflow and not a dependency chain. It uses the official ITIL 4 management-practices framing as the reference catalogue anchor.

model_dimensions.title: Service Lifecycle Flow
model_dimensions.intent: Shows system, value-chain, and lifecycle behavior through reference flow models.
model_dimensions.notes: Detailed descriptions and contribution mappings are not loaded yet.

model_dimensions.title: Practice Contribution Map
model_dimensions.intent: Maps practices to value-chain activities, value streams, and flow nodes.
model_dimensions.notes: Do not infer these mappings from list order. Load only when the mapping basis is explicit, or keep the entry empty.

model_dimensions.title: Reference Dependency Graph
model_dimensions.intent: Represents dependency relationships implied by contribution, value-stream, data-object, or functional-component structure when explicit relationships are loaded.
model_dimensions.notes: No dependency edge is asserted until the relationship basis is explicit.

node_types.title: Framework
node_types.intent: The top-level operating-model frame that explains the purpose, scope, and navigation logic of STS.
node_types.guidance: Define what operating model is being explored, why it exists, and what learning path it gives to the reader.

node_types.title: Model Root
node_types.guidance: Use model roots to separate the outer operating model from the inner managed service model.

node_types.title: Model Domain
node_types.intent: A major domain inside a model root.
node_types.guidance: Use model domains to give each root a practical drill-down structure before detailed workflows are modeled.

node_types.title: Practice Group
node_types.intent: A recognized family of practices used to organize ITSM concerns at the highest level.
node_types.guidance: Use practice groups to orient readers before they drill into individual practices.

node_types.title: Practice
node_types.intent: A recognized management concern such as Change Enablement, Incident Management, or Service Catalogue Management.
node_types.guidance: Each practice can later decompose into workflow variants, buckets, artifacts, discipline mappings, and maturity targets, but the current reference node must preserve the external practice meaning.

node_types.title: Flow Model
node_types.intent: A lifecycle, value-chain, value-stream, or system model that explains runtime behavior beyond a catalogue list.
node_types.guidance: Check whether the model is a strict workflow, a value stream, a system map, or a non-linear activity model before drawing sequence arrows.

node_types.title: Flow Component
node_types.intent: A structural component inside a system-level model.
node_types.guidance: Use for system positioning, inputs, outputs, governance components, or reference components that are not workflow activities.

node_types.title: Flow Activity
node_types.intent: An activity inside a lifecycle or value-chain model.
node_types.guidance: Use for named activities where the reference framework defines behavior, not just taxonomy.

node_types.title: Value Stream
node_types.intent: A named stream of work, information, or value movement across a management lifecycle.
node_types.guidance: Use for externally defined value streams. Local value streams are deferred and must be explicitly labeled when introduced.

model_roots.title: Model Roots
model_roots.intent: Start with the STS Operating Model for the shared-services ecosystem, then use the STS Managed Service Model to look inside one service.

flow_models.title: Shared Technology Services (STS) Framework Journey
flow_models.intent: Follow the service-management journey through ITIL and IT4IT lifecycle structures before drilling into practices.

model_dimensions.title: Journey Lenses
model_dimensions.intent: Use separate lenses for catalogue order, lifecycle flow, contribution mapping, and dependency analysis so the journey is not reduced to a table of contents.

framework_map.title: Practice Catalogue
framework_map.intent: Use the catalogue as the recognized ITIL vocabulary for capabilities that participate in the service journey. It is not a process sequence by itself.

practice_groups.title: Practice Groups
practice_groups.intent: The top-level ITIL management-practice families used to orient the reference model.

practices.title: Practices
practices.intent: The recognized ITIL practice areas. Deeper workflows, artifacts, evidence, and maturity remain outside the current reference layer until they are explicitly modeled.

model.title: Model Construct
model.intent: The graph stores both content and the guidance used to author that content.

guidance.title: Guidance Questions
guidance.intent: The questions that turn the database into a guiding system rather than passive storage.

guidance_questions.question: Does this root explain the STS ecosystem or the internal structure of one service?
guidance_questions.intent: Separate outer operating-model concerns from inner managed-service concerns.
guidance_questions.guidance: A root should make the level of analysis obvious before any practice or workflow mapping is shown.

guidance_questions.question: Is this activity ordered, iterative, optional, or combined differently per value stream?
guidance_questions.guidance: Use edge metadata to distinguish strict sequence from reference order.

guidance_questions.question: What family of operating concerns does this group hold?
guidance_questions.intent: Clarify why practices are grouped together.
guidance_questions.guidance: A practice group should help navigation, not become a separate governance layer.

guidance_questions.question: What operating model is being defined and what is intentionally outside its scope?
guidance_questions.intent: Clarify the boundary of the framework.
guidance_questions.guidance: A framework without boundaries becomes a generic encyclopedia rather than a usable operating model.

guidance_questions.question: What outcome must this practice achieve in the service-management reference context?
guidance_questions.intent: Define the practice outcome before artifacts.
guidance_questions.guidance: Start from the reference outcome so later workflow and artifact choices do not become tool-driven.

guidance_questions.question: What role does this component play in the reference system model?
guidance_questions.intent: Separates structural positioning from workflow execution.
guidance_questions.guidance: Use components for inputs, governance, practices, improvement, value outputs, and other non-activity parts.

guidance_questions.question: What value or information movement does this stream represent?
guidance_questions.intent: Makes value streams practical while staying tied to their reference model.
guidance_questions.guidance: Detailed activities, data objects, and functional components should be loaded when the modeling basis is explicit.

guidance_questions.question: Which operating concern or managed service anatomy area does this domain organize?
guidance_questions.intent: Make each domain a practical home for related information.
guidance_questions.guidance: A domain should be broad enough to maintain but specific enough that readers know what belongs there.

guidance_questions.question: Which reference model defines this flow model?
guidance_questions.intent: Keeps industry flows tied to their reference model.
guidance_questions.guidance: Record the model name, behavior kind, and the description chosen for publication.

guidance_questions.question: How does this root connect to ITIL practices, IT4IT value streams, SRE, DevSecOps, and tooling views?
guidance_questions.intent: Keep reference frameworks as overlays instead of confusing them with the STS model itself.
guidance_questions.guidance: Describe the root in STS terms, then map practices and disciplines into it.

guidance_questions.question: Is this a workflow, lifecycle, value chain, value stream, system map, or state model?
guidance_questions.intent: Prevents accidental conversion of non-linear frameworks into false linear workflows.
guidance_questions.guidance: Declare the behavior kind before adding edges or sequence diagrams.

guidance_questions.question: What learning path should a reader follow from high-level concept to practical artifact?
guidance_questions.guidance: The site should help a user move from concept to detail without losing context.

guidance_questions.question: Which services, managed elements, cycles, artifacts, evidence, metrics, or owners belong under this domain?
guidance_questions.intent: Prepare the domain for later workflow and artifact drilldown.
guidance_questions.guidance: Use the domain to anchor future lower-level records without overloading the root page.

guidance_questions.question: Which workflow variants, buckets, artifacts, and decisions are required to make this practice real?
guidance_questions.guidance: A practice is not complete until it can be decomposed into actions, objects, evidence, and ownership.

urn:sts:framework:shared-technology-serv.title: Authority boundary
urn:sts:framework:shared-technology-serv.body: Current reference mode preserves external standards and named disciplines in their own vocabulary, structure, and recognized meaning. Local operating-model extensions are deferred and must be modeled separately from external reference truth.

urn:sts:framework:shared-technology-serv.title: Ordering boundary
urn:sts:framework:shared-technology-serv.body: Every graph node has deterministic ordering inside its scope. External reference nodes follow reference-list ordering; where the reference provides a list but not a workflow, the order must be labeled as list order. Site navigation order is only display metadata and must not be treated as industry sequence.

urn:sts:framework:shared-technology-serv.title: Flow and lifecycle layer
urn:sts:framework:shared-technology-serv.body: Practice catalogues define vocabulary. Flow models, value streams, activities, edges, and positionings explain how service-management behavior works end to end. Current flow nodes preserve external ITIL and IT4IT reference structure only.

urn:sts:framework:shared-technology-serv.title: Multidimensional operating model
urn:sts:framework:shared-technology-serv.body: The same practice can belong to multiple industry-reference dimensions: reference catalogue, lifecycle flow, contribution map, and empty dependency graph. Local rollout, maturity, assurance, and bank-specific interpretations remain out of scope until the ITIL / ITSM / IT4IT reference abstraction is stable.
